scope: Theorem 1.1 (Prescribed boundary endpoints) of the manuscript “Critical honeycomb chords with prescribed boundary endpoints” (preprints/Critical-honeycomb-chords-with-prescribed-boundary-endpoints-September-26-2026/main.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 237 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 6b7adfc0aa278ae3), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF pages 2-3. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. The quote crosses a page break and includes whatever the extraction places there, such as a page number. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let DR be convex pure lattice hexagons which, after scaling by R, converge to a regular hexagon. Let aR, bR be boundary ports whose scaled limits are distinct points in the relative interiors of sides. Then, for every ε > 0, the critical chord law satisfies PDR;aR,bR {R4/3−ε ≤ L(γ) ≤ R4/3+ε } −→ 1. The same conclusion holds in a full half-plane for prescribed boundary ports at distance R, in a strip of height comparable to R for one prescribed port on each of the two opposite boundary cuts, at 2 mutual distance O(R), and in a wedge of angle π/3 or 2π/3 formed by two nonparallel pure cuts, with one prescribed port on each ray. In the wedge, each endpoint has clearance comparable to R from the other cut and distance O(R) from the apex. Constants are uniform on fixed compact sets of these nondegenerate scaled geometries. In each case the normalizing mass is at least cR−5/4.
